notes: Website for Desert Elite Homes & Construction, a custom home builder in Scottsdale, Arizona (custom homes, renovations, room additions, kitchen and bath, lot and land development, project management). All the words, links and photo descriptions are in small files in src/data, and the pages only draw them, so change content in the data files and leave everything else alone. src/data/site.ts: the business name, the licence number (353956), the areas served, the Instagram link. src/data/nav.ts: the menu and the quote button. src/data/footer.ts: the footer words. src/data/pages.ts: for each page, the tab title and the description search engines show (keep a title under 70 characters and a description under 200). src/data/services.ts: the six services, in the order the Services page shows them. Each service is written once and used in four places: its card on the home page (shortName, icon, cardText), its section on the Services page (name, eyebrow, paragraphs, list, buttonLabel), its link in the footer (footerLabel) and what search engines read (schemaDescription). Never change a service id. To add to a service's list, add one line to its list. src/data/home.ts: the home page (hero, trust bar, headings, the numbers that count up in stats, three recent-work photos, the six process steps, the closing call to action). src/data/about.ts: the About page. src/data/servicesPage.ts: the Why Desert Elite cells and the closing call to action on the Services page. src/data/projects.ts: the Gallery page (the filter buttons, the tiles, the note under them). src/data/contact.ts: the words on the Contact page (not the form). src/data/notFound.ts: the page for a missing address. In the words, [[gold words]] show in the gold highlight, {br} is a line break and {br-desktop} a line break on wide screens only: keep these marks when you edit around them. Every photo is listed once in src/data/pictures.ts with its file and a description, and the pages refer to it by id (for example { picture: "kitchen-1" }). A place may give its own alt only when it needs a different description. Photos are .jpg files in public/images. You can replace an existing .jpg with an attached photo (it keeps its file name, and the .webp copy is made at build time), and then you must update that photo's description in src/data/pictures.ts. You can add an attached photo to the gallery with add_image: choose a short name, add it to src/data/pictures.ts (src "/images/name.jpg" and a description), then add one entry at the end of items in src/data/projects.ts that refers to it with a category (custom, renovation or kitchen), a type, a title, and layout "featured". Photos on the site are shown in frames that crop them, so say in the summary that a photo of a different shape may be trimmed. The same facts appear in more than one place on purpose: the years in business (38) is in src/data/home.ts stats and in src/data/about.ts (the badge and the story paragraph), and the licence number is in src/data/site.ts, src/data/home.ts, src/data/about.ts, src/data/servicesPage.ts and src/data/pages.ts. When asked to change a fact like that, search for every place and change them all in one request, and if it would need more than five files, change what you can and say what is left. These are business and legal claims (licensed, bonded, insured, years of experience, the ROC number): change them only when the client states the new fact, never invent or round them. The site shows no phone number or email today, only the contact form: if asked to add one and the client gives none, open no PR and ask for it. You cannot edit the contact form, the privacy policy, the page layouts, the styles, the scripts or the sitemap. For those, and for a new page, a new kind of section, a blog, a booking calendar or a new form field, open no PR and say it needs a person. The copyright year in the footer is a launch year that the page updates itself into a range, so if asked to change it, open no PR and say it already updates itself. Do not change colours, fonts or layout classes. Do not invent prices, phone numbers, addresses, awards or claims that the client did not give you.
